source: USGS Unified Geologic Map of the Moon, 1:5,000,000 (Fortezzo, Spudis and Harrel 2020)
note: Map unit of the smallest polygon containing the app's target coordinates. Regional context; it does not resolve pits, caves, ice or the exact landing area.

unit.name: Eratosthenian Crater
unit.description: Non-rayed, circular craters with sharp to partially subdued crater rim crests, partial circumferential ejecta present, and lower albedo compared to unit Cc.
unit.interpretation: Morphology and material from a primary impact event.

unit.name: pre-Nectarian Basin Massif
unit.description: Large mountainous landforms commonly lying along arc, both continuous and discontinuous, gradational with generally finer-scale topography.
unit.interpretation: Uplifted bedrock during the formation of basins.

unit.name: Eratosthenian Imbrian Plateau
unit.description: Forms high standing plateaus (relative to the mare surfaces in Oceanus Procellarum) with domes, cones, and dark mantling materials.
unit.interpretation: Volcanic constructs, flows, and pyroclastic materials.

unit.name: Imbrian Mare, Upper
unit.description: Forms flat, smooth surfaces. Lower albedo and crater density than unit Im1. Numerous ridges. Difficult to distinguish from unit Id.

unit.name: Imbrian Plains
unit.description: Smooth, flat to undulatory terrain of intermediate albedo occurring mostly in topographic lows and crater floors of Imbrian and older age.
unit.interpretation: Ambiguous origin, likely Orientale and other large impact crater ejecta.
